clue.text: Succulent cabbage stuffed with dried chilli pepper

indicators.note: a thing stuffed with something has that filling packed inside it

blocks.note: kale is a kind of cabbage
an ancho is a dried poblano chilli

explanation.surface: A recipe for a stuffed cabbage, spiced with dried chilli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succulent' looks like praise for the dish, but it is the noun: a fleshy-leaved plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalanchoe is a genus of fleshy-leaved plants, so it is an example of a succulent.

clue.text: SI unit, kelvin? Almost in any circumstances

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: K is the symbol for kelvin
'at all' means in any circumstances

explanation.surface: A query whether the kelvin is an SI unit, answered with 'pretty much always'.
explanation.walkthrough: The kelvin really is an SI unit, so it looks like the definition; it only supplies K.
explanation.definitionFit: The katal is the SI unit of catalytic activity, one mole per second.

clue.text: E. African patriarch, one clad in goat’s hair

indicators.note: being clad in something means being wrapped inside it

blocks.note: aba is a coarse cloth woven from goat or camel hair
'un is a dialect form of one

explanation.surface: An Ethiopian church leader, dressed in a goat-hair robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuna is the title of the patriarch heading the Ethiopian Orthodox Church, in East Africa.

clue.text: Tumour, forming soft ring in bean

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the bean word

blocks.note: a lima bean
p for piano, soft in music
a ring is shaped like O

explanation.surface: A growth forming a soft ring inside a bean pod.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipoma is a benign tumour made of fatty tissue, usually under the skin.

clue.text: Everyone basking perhaps turned up in Indian streams

indicators.note: a creature basking lies in the sun, so the group word sits inside it
in a down entry, turning something up reads it from the bottom back to the top

blocks.note: everyone is all
the sun is what one might be basking in, so perhaps hints at that

explanation.surface: A crowd of sunbathers appears beside rivers in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basking' means being in the sun, so it both signals the enclosing and implies the sun itself; 'perhaps' admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A nulla or nullah is an Indian word for a watercourse or ravine, so nullas are streams there.

clue.text: Second-rate judge, US creature accepting international case mostly

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the following letters go inside
mostly means not all, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: critter is American dialect for creature
I is the abbreviation for international
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor-quality judge: an American creature taking on an international case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' suggests the courtroom, but this is a literary judge, a critic.
explanation.definitionFit: A criticaster is a petty or inferior critic, the -aster suffix meaning a poor imitation.

clue.text: Clumsy types taking hold of amateur fundamentalist group

indicators.note: taking hold of something means gripping it, so it is held within

blocks.note: hams are overacting, clumsy performers
A is the abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: Bumbling people seize an amateur fundamentalist outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamas is the Palestinian Islamist movement, an Islamic fundamentalist organisation.

clue.text: To assert a basic norm, incline prop that’s shifted (11, two words)

indicators.note: something shifted is moved about, so these letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Building advice: a support for a slope has moved, so a basic rule needs restating.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on principle means doing it because of a fundamental rule or belief, asserting that norm.

clue.text: Tense before ceremony, rinky-dink

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Nerves before a ceremony that turns out to be small-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like nervous, but it is the grammar term giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Rinky-dink is American slang for cheap, corny or hackneyed, which matches trite.

clue.text: Odd characters in fling, so displaying sign of contempt once

indicators.note: the odd characters are those in first, third, fifth and seventh positions

blocks.note: every other letter starting from the first

explanation.surface: Strange people at a fling give a rude gesture of disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: A figo is an archaic name for the fig, a rude gesture made with the thumb between two fingers to show scorn.

clue.text: Premature canine’s development

indicators.note: a development is a change in form, so the letters change their arrangement

blocks.note: the dog word without its possessive ending

explanation.surface: A puppy that has grown up too early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanic describes the youthful stage of an animal's growth before maturity, an immature or premature phase.

clue.text: Flight from France for somewhere else to the east thereof

definitions.text: somewhere else to the east thereof

blocks.note: first meaning: an archaic word for a flight of steps

blocks.clueFragment: somewhere else to the east thereof
blocks.note: second meaning: a country lying east of France

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight from France' suggests escape; the clue swaps that country for one to its east, which is also an old word for a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a country east of France, and greece, also spelt grece, is an obsolete word for steps or a stair.

clue.text: School finals, rather a filler?

blocks.note: 'a bit' means rather, as in 'a bit cold'
'ur' is a hesitation sound used to fill a pause in speech

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that school finals are just something to fill time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'filler' means a word filling a pause in speech. The Abitur is the German school-leaving examination.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abitur is the final examination taken at the end of secondary school in Germany, qualifying for university.

clue.text: Rearing boils, increasingly inflamed

indicators.note: something that boils churns about, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical note: the boils are rising up and getting more inflamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boils' reads as a noun, the skin sores, but works as a verb signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry describes skin that is red and inflamed, so angrier is a comparative meaning more inflamed.

clue.text: Amazonian monkey found on island

blocks.note: a monkey is the heavy falling weight of a pile-driver, also called a tup
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A naturalist reports a monkey from the Amazon discovered on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' is not the animal but the ram of a pile-driver; 'Amazonian' is a noun for a person of the Amazon region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tupi are an indigenous people of the Amazon basin, so a Tupi is a native Amazonian.

clue.text: Roman chariots, grand, of an appropriate age

blocks.note: grand in the sense of large
ae. abbreviates Latin aetatis, of age, a fitting language for Romans

explanation.surface: Splendid old Roman chariots described as being of a suitable vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin abbreviation is 'appropriate' because the answer is itself Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigae is the Latin plural for two-horse chariots used by the ancient Romans in races.

clue.text: Consecrated slab varying astral timbre (10, two words)

indicators.note: varying means changing, so the letters change their order

blocks.note: taken as written
timbre is the tone or quality of a sound

explanation.surface: A sacred stone gives off an otherworldly, shifting sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar stone is the blessed stone slab set into or forming an altar, consecrated for the Mass.

clue.text: Witch or priest assimilating the ego

indicators.note: to assimilate is to take in and absorb, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: A choice between a witch and a priest who has absorbed someone's ego.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamia is a female demon or sorceress of classical legend, hence a witch.

clue.text: Typical of mermaid in South Pacific

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
irenic means peaceable, a synonym of pacific

explanation.surface: A mermaid, characteristically, found in the South Pacific ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' seems to be the ocean, but it is the adjective meaning peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirens were seductive sea-singers akin to mermaids, so sirenic describes what is characteristic of one.

clue.text: Number in fantastic dance centres displaying superiority

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A routine in some amazing dance studios shows off real excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a dance routine, but it is just the abbreviation N, joining the other letters before they are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Transcendence is the state of surpassing or rising above others, which is a form of superiority.

clue.text: Wee one’s Xmas present, parts of it missing? He’ll go through it

indicators.note: with parts missing, some letters are taken out of the toy

blocks.note: a train set, a typical present for a small child

explanation.surface: A toddler's Christmas train set has bits missing, and he will play with it anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The I and T are removed. Transe is a Scots word for a passage or corridor, which a person goes through.
explanation.definitionFit: A transe in Scots is an entrance passage or lobby, something a person walks through.

clue.text: Matters to confer on getting them informally in rising commotion

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up
the commotion word gets, or takes in, the informal pronoun

blocks.note: a stir is a commotion
'em is casual speech for them

explanation.surface: Things to discuss with them casually amid growing uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Remits are matters referred to a committee or body for consideration and decision.

clue.text: Number fatten up in acrylic fabric

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
to lard is to fatten

explanation.surface: A garment made of synthetic fabric that bulks up its wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dralon is a trademark acrylic fibre used for upholstery and clothing fabric.

clue.text: I’ll be induced by free entry for cabaret

indicators.note: letters set free are loose to fall into any order
induced here means led in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: the speaker's I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A promise to be lured into a nightclub by free admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitery is a slangy term for a nightclub, a venue offering cabaret entertainment.

clue.text: Lively dances? Further attempt is past

blocks.note: a redo is another go
was is the past tense of is

explanation.surface: Someone asks for another go at the lively dances, but that moment has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The redowa is a lively Bohemian couple dance resembling a waltz or polka, so redowas are such dances.

clue.text: With which Paddy bemoans being single around house

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: single means one
ho. is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: An Irishman laments that he is unmarried and lives alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy is a traditional nickname for an Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohone is an Irish and Scots exclamation of grief, used when lamenting.

clue.text: A portion of strawberry ice cream, teatime treat?

indicators.note: a small portion of a word here means just its opening letter

blocks.note: its initial letter
an ice cream served in a cone

explanation.surface: A serving of strawberry ice cream offered as an afternoon snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A scone with strawberry jam and clotted cream is the classic British cream tea, so the surface paints the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small baked cake served at British afternoon tea, a classic teatime snack.

clue.text: Gentle massage one’s given to king, held in check, not new

indicators.note: given to means placed against, so one letter sits just before the other
something held in is enclosed, so the pair goes inside the rein word
'not' tells us to drop the letter standing for new

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
K is the chess abbreviation for king
to rein is to check or restrain
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A masseur's gentle treatment for a king, who is restrained and no longer fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' sounds like a test, but it is the verb restrain; the pair sits after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiki is a Japanese healing therapy using light touch, loosely a gentle hands-on massage.

clue.text: Ancient prayer from Galloway etc incorporating religious teaching

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: kye is Scots for cattle, and Galloway is a breed of cattle
RI stands for religious instruction

explanation.surface: An old prayer from south-west Scotland that carries religious instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Galloway' looks like the Scottish region, but here it is the breed of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kyrie eleison is an ancient Greek petition for mercy used in Christian liturgy.

clue.text: Poet’s difficult to understand, first to last, making one annoyed

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved to the end of the word

blocks.note: dirke is Spenser's spelling of dark, obscure

explanation.surface: An obscure poet's work is irritating readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet' in Azed usually means Spenser; his dirke means dark, here obscure in meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Irked means annoyed or irritated, a direct synonym describing someone vexed.

clue.text: China map is wrong for one dwelling in the tropics

indicators.note: if the letters are wrong they must be put right by rearranging them

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A map of China is mistaken about where a tropical resident lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphiscians are tropical inhabitants whose noon shadows fall north or south according to season.

clue.text: Formless basis for braided material

indicators.note: less signals taking away, here the shape word given before it

blocks.note: a platform is a basis or foundation

explanation.surface: A shapeless foundation for a plaited textile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formless' reads as shapeless, but it is FORM plus less, removing those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plat is a plait, a strip of braided straw or other material.

clue.text: Sudanese possibly in love, reverse of forward

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: love is nil, a zero score
to as an adverb can mean forward, as in 'heave to'

explanation.surface: A Sudanese person falling in love, then backing away from making advances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like the opposite of reverse, but it is a word to be reversed itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nilot is a member of the Nile-valley peoples, many living in South Sudan, so a Sudanese is one example.

clue.text: Coffee maker, no longer brisk

blocks.note: first meaning: short for percolator
second meaning: an obsolete adjective for lively or brisk

explanation.surface: A coffee machine that has lost its pep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the second meaning as obsolete; it is not a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is informal for a percolator, and in older English perk meant lively, smart or brisk.

clue.text: Jock’s bound to hold and be steadfast as once

indicators.note: the bounding word holds the other word inside it

blocks.note: sten is Scots for leap or bound; Jock means a Scot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is obliged to hold firm and stay loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like obliged, but in Scots it is a leap. 'As once' marks an archaic form.
explanation.definitionFit: Standen is an old plural or infinitive form of stand, so it once meant to stand firm.

clue.text: Scottish Charley, left drooping locally

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
owrie is a Scots dialect word for drooping or dismal

explanation.surface: A Scottish man named Charley has been left feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: Charley is an old name for a fox; in Scotland the fox is called Lowrie, and 'locally' marks the dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowrie or Lowrie Tod is the Scots folk name for the fox, which in England is Charley.

clue.text: Longing to return east in grip of craving, jealous

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
being in the grip of something means being held inside it

blocks.note: a yen is a longing
E is the abbreviation for east
greed is a craving

explanation.surface: Wanting to go back east while gripped by desire and envy.
explanation.definitionFit: Green-eyed is the stock adjective for envious, from Shakespeare's 'green-eyed monster' of jealousy.
